terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the sweep measures retrieval on the labelled questions.

tasks.title: Hit rate and recall at k
tasks.description:
Implement two functions in `src/metrics.ts`. Each takes `results: Retrieval[]`, where a `Retrieval` is `{ expected, retrieved }`: the article ids that answer a question, and the article ids of its hits in rank order (repeats are possible). Only the first `k` retrieved ids count.

- `hitRate(results, k)`: the share of questions with at least one expected id in the top `k`.
- `recallAtK(results, k)`: for each question, the share of its expected ids found in the top `k`, counting each id once; then the average over all questions.
- Both return `0` for an empty list.

The check runs both on a hidden set of results at several values of `k`, including repeated ids and an empty list.
nextSteps: Work out the hit rate and recall of a two-question example on paper.
Write hitRate with the top k ids of each question.
Write recallAtK the same way, one score per question, then average.
Handle the empty list in both.
hints: Slicing retrieved from 0 to k gives the ids that count.
A question that expects two articles and finds one has recall 0.5 and is still a hit.
Put the top k ids in a Set and count how many expected ids it has. That way a repeated id cannot count twice.

tasks.title: Run the labelled questions
tasks.description:
Implement `evaluate(settings, questions = labelled, client)` in `src/evaluate.ts`. It returns `Promise<{ hitRate, recall }>`:

- Chunk the handbook with `settings.chunkSize` and `settings.overlap` and index the chunks.
- Search each question with `settings.k` and no minimum score.
- Build one `Retrieval` per question: `expected` from the label, `retrieved` as the `source` of each hit (the article id, not the chunk id), in rank order.
- Return `hitRate` and `recallAtK` of those results at `settings.k`.

Use the parameters, not the values in `config.ts`. The check compares your scores with the correct ones for several settings and for a shorter list of questions.
nextSteps: Build the index once from the settings.
Loop over the questions and search each one.
Map each question's hits to article ids.
Return both metrics and run `node src/sweep.ts`.
hints: chunkDocs, indexChunks and search are already in the workspace and work as in earlier issues.
Labels name articles, such as 'weather'. A chunk id like 'weather#1' never equals 'weather', which would make every score 0.
For each question, keep its expected list next to the source of each of its hits. After the loop, pass all of them and settings.k to both metrics.

tasks.title: Find and fix the bad setting
tasks.description:
The answer box runs with the settings in `src/config.ts`, and one of them is hurting retrieval. Use `node src/sweep.ts` to measure, then fix `config.ts`.

Team limits:

- `TOP_K` from 1 to 3: the prompt has room for three passages.
- `CHUNK_SIZE` from 1 to 500 characters.
- `CHUNK_OVERLAP` from 0 up to less than `CHUNK_SIZE`.

Goal: every labelled question finds all of its articles, so hit rate and recall are both 100%. The check measures your settings with a correct `evaluate`, and type-checks `config.ts`, `evaluate.ts` and `metrics.ts`.
nextSteps: Run `node src/sweep.ts` and read the line for config.ts.
Compare it with the rows of the grid below it.
Change the setting the numbers point at, and run the sweep again.
hints: TOP_K is already at the team limit, so the fix is not a bigger k.
Read the chunks that 20 characters gives you in your head: how many words fit in one?
Pick a chunk size, with some overlap, whose k=3 column reads 100% for both numbers, then run the sweep to confirm it.
